title: Single and double circuits
caption: Count three phase positions per circuit. The upper earth wire is a shield wire, not a fourth phase.

title: Single, double and multiple circuits
caption: The photographs connect the circuit count to actual tower construction.

title: Solid and stranded conductors
caption: Stranding provides flexibility. It does not eliminate skin effect; compare with Section~\ref{resistance}.

title: Steel and composite cores
caption: Recognize the load-bearing core and surrounding aluminium strands. Composite cores are class context.

title: ACSR cross-section
caption: The steel core supplies tensile strength; aluminium carries most of the load current.

title: Current penetration
caption: The darkened conducting regions are a qualitative sketch: current density varies continuously, not as a sharp hollow cylinder.

title: Magnetic loops
caption: Circular flux paths around a long conductor explain the Ampere-law integration.

title: Internal and external flux
caption: Internal flux links only a fraction of the total current; external flux links all the conductor current.

title: Internal cylindrical shell
caption: Identify shell radius x, thickness dx and the fraction of current enclosed.

title: External cylindrical shell
caption: Integrate the external field between the conductor surface and the return-path distance.

title: Flux linkage with a reference point
caption: Each other conductor contributes a logarithmic distance term; the sum of balanced currents removes the remote reference.

title: Composite conductor groups
caption: Use every cross-group pair for mutual GMD and all ordered within-group pairs for self GMD.

title: Three-phase transposition
caption: Each phase occupies each physical position for one third of a full transposition cycle.

title: Hexagon and tower arrangements
caption: The geometrical conductor diagram is the electrical model; the tower is its physical support.

title: All three double-circuit positions
caption: Track phase partners through all three positions. Take the geometric mean of their group quantities; do not average distances arithmetically.

title: Bundle spacers and suspension
caption: Subconductors of a bundle belong to one phase. The spacer fixes bundle geometry; circuit count is a separate idea.

title: Radial electric field
caption: Gauss law gives E proportional to 1/x outside a long round conductor. Potential is the integral of this field.

title: Phase and earth capacitance
caption: This is a conceptual sketch. Use the balanced per-phase model and image-conductor derivation in Section~\ref{capacitance} for calculations.

title: Potential between radii
caption: Only potential differences are finite for an isolated infinite line charge. Do not set its potential at infinity to zero.

title: Superposition of line charges
caption: Sum the potential contributions of all charges before using balanced-charge cancellation.

title: Two-wire charges
caption: Opposite charges set the phase-to-phase voltage; the capacitance to neutral is twice the two-wire capacitance.

title: Short-line equivalent
caption: Series Z remains; shunt admittance is neglected. The nominal-T and nominal-pi models are redrawn in Section~\ref{models}.

title: Distributed line
caption: A small segment contains series resistance and inductance and shunt conductance and capacitance. The continuous limit produces the long-line equations.

title: Open-circuit terminal condition
caption: Set receiving current to zero to identify A and C. Port current directions must match the ABCD definition.

title: Short-circuit terminal condition
caption: Set receiving voltage to zero to identify B and D. This is a parameter-identification condition, not normal loading.

title: Cascade connection
caption: The output of one network drives the input of the next. Multiply ABCD matrices in their physical order.

title: Parallel connection
caption: Both networks share corresponding port voltages. Add admittance matrices, not ABCD matrices.

title: Skin-effect sections
caption: Inner filaments link more magnetic flux. The hollow-looking conducting region is a qualitative high-frequency picture.

title: Ferranti physical picture
caption: At no load, distributed charging current still flows and the receiving voltage can exceed sending voltage.

title: Ferranti phasors
caption: With receiving voltage as reference, charging current leads by 90 degrees. The reactive series voltage points opposite to receiving voltage; resistive voltage follows charging current.

title: Ferranti waveforms
caption: The voltage rise is explained by phasor addition. Use the half-length charging-current approximation in the main derivation; a lumped total current gives the wrong factor.

title: Corona on fittings
caption: The class photograph illustrates visible discharge at regions of high surface electric field.

title: Corona along a line
caption: Violet glow is a recognition aid; inception depends on geometry, surface condition and atmosphere, not a universal voltage threshold.

title: Insulator type gallery
caption: Recognize glass/disc, post, pin, shackle, strain, stay and suspension forms. The four syllabus-focused forms are explained in the main text.

title: Mechanical string and electrical equivalent
caption: Match metal links to shunt capacitances, and each insulating disc to series capacitance. Arcing horns provide a controlled external flashover path.

title: Four-disc string and earth capacitance
caption: Equal series discs do not give equal voltages when their junctions have earth capacitance. Disc voltage rises towards the conductor.

title: Capacitance grading circuit
caption: Different disc capacitances give equal intended disc voltages. The caption C1 on the shunt branches refers to the top-unit reference capacitance.
